chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the child who chooses polytheism while he is between his two parents, he said: 'He is not left (alone), and that is when one of his parents is a Christian.'

key_terms.بَيْنَ أَبَوَيْهِ: Between his two parents (under their guardianship)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a child who chooses polytheism when one parent is Christian?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a young child who chooses polytheism (shirk) is not left in that state if one parent is Christian, indicating a specific legal mechanism for managing the apostasy of minors under mixed or non-Muslim guardianship. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic distinction between the innate fitrah of the child and the external influence of the parent, ensuring the child's religious status is actively managed rather than passively accepted. The context underscores the importance of parental lineage in determining the child's initial religious identity and the procedures for correcting deviation during minority.
